question: A 64-year-old T2DM patient has HbA1c 8.1% on metformin and has established coronary artery disease (post-MI 2 years ago). Which additional antidiabetic agent has the strongest evidence for cardiovascular mortality reduction in this patient?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Sulphonylureas lower glucose but have NOT demonstrated cardiovascular mortality reduction in outcome trials. Some earlier data raised safety concerns.
Pioglitazone has some cardiovascular data (PROactive trial) but is not first-choice in post-MI patients and is associated with heart failure risk and bladder cancer concerns.

Correct. The EMPA-REG OUTCOME trial demonstrated that empagliflozin reduced cardiovascular mortality by 38% and heart failure hospitalisations in T2DM patients with established CVD. GLP-1 agonists (e.g., liraglutide, semaglutide) are an equally valid first choice per ADA 2024.
DPP-4 inhibitors are cardiovascular neutral (non-inferior, not superior). Sitagliptin does not reduce cardiovascular mortality, though it is safe in CVD.

overallFeedback.feedback: In T2DM with established CVD, use agents with proven cardiovascular outcome benefit: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin — EMPA-REG; dapagliflozin — DECLARE) and GLP-1 RAs (liraglutide — LEADER; semaglutide — SUSTAIN-6).
Well done — SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists with proven CVD benefit are preferred add-on agents in T2DM patients with established cardiovascular disease.
